    Pneumonitis (Pneumonia)
      Classification
        Bacterial Pneumonia
          Lobar pneumonia

            Viruses

            Mycoplasma pneumonia
            Undefined agents
    Lobar Pneumonia
      Definition
        Entire lung lobe infection
        95% Streptococcus pneumoniae
      Characteristics
        Middle-aged males
        Droplet infection
      Pathogenesis
        1. Pneumococci inhaled
        2. Settle in lower lobes
        3. Inflammatory reaction
        4. Spread via inter-alveolar pores
        5. Lung consolidation
      Stages
        1. Congestion (Day 1)
        2. Red Hepatization (Days 2-4)
        3. Gray Hepatization (Days 5-8)
        4. Resolution (Days 9-21)
      Complications
        Pulmonary
          Delayed resolution
          Fibrosis
          Lung abscess
        Extra-pulmonary
          Pleural infections
          Organ spread
          Cardiac toxicity
    Bacterial Bronchopneumonia
      Definition
        Bronchioles + alveoli infection
        Patchy consolidation
      Types
        Primary
          Exogenous invaders
          Extremes of age
        Secondary
          Post-infective
          Aspiration
          Hypostatic
          Terminal
      Common Organisms
        Staphylococcus aureus
        Streptococcus pyogenes
        Pneumococcus
        H. influenzae
    Bronchiectasis
      Definition
        Permanent bronchial dilation
      Characteristics
        Males <20 years
        Chronic pyogenic infection
    Lung Abscess
      Definition
        Localized suppuration
      Causes
        Inhalation
        Pyemic spread
        Post-pneumonic
        Secondary infection
        Trauma
    Pleural Diseases
      Pleuritis (Pleurisy)
        Causes
          Infective
            Bacteria
            Viruses
            Fungi
          Non-infective
            Collagen diseases
            Trauma
            Tumors
        Types
          Acute Serofibrinous
          Suppurative (Empyema)
            Pyogenic bacteria
            Diffuse/Localized
